pre_live_amendments.reason: the first live-06 pair exposed that the host-owned Next.js production-build step denied loopback bind even though Turbopack may require an internal loopback port during build; it also exposed that requiring every baseline to reach completion verification contradicts the frozen v4 rule that honest baseline failures remain in the denominator and are never overridden
pre_live_amendments.change: allow loopback only, while retaining the external-network deny, for the host-owned production-build step; require every baseline to bind the task contract, discover its product run, and record either a completion-verification attempt or a discovered nonzero product failure as an honest terminal
pre_live_amendments.exclusion_rule_changes: none; honest early baseline failures remain included
pre_live_amendments.superseded_evidence_policy: retain live-06 as immutable one-pair instrument-defect evidence; do not resume, rescore, reuse proposals, or include it in live-07 quality inference

pre_live_amendments.reason: the first live-07 pair and an isolated workspace-copy diagnostic proved that allowing 127.0.0.1 loopback did not cover the bind used internally by Next.js 16 Turbopack; switching to the official webpack production-build path removed that bind, after which child cleanup required signals that the default-deny profile had not allowed
pre_live_amendments.change: use the host-owned direct argv ["npx","next","build","--webpack"] before ["npx","next","start","-p","<port>"]; deny all build network operations; allow signals only when the target is in the same macOS sandbox so candidate processes cannot signal host processes

pre_live_amendments.superseded_evidence_policy: retain live-07 as immutable one-pair instrument-defect evidence; do not resume, rescore, reuse proposals, or include it in live-08 quality inference
